title: Deep-learning fiber-force microscopy reveals how cells pull on fibrous environments
summary: Deep-learning-enabled live-cell fiber-force microscopy (DLFM) computes forces that cells exert on tissue-like fiber networks from phase microscopy, tracking cell movement and fiber deformation without fluorescent labels. It showed ten-fold changes in force as cells change shape during migration, force dipoles in cell-cell interactions, and altered force patterns during stem cell differentiation. Experiments and modelling indicate cells form force-generating adhesions throughout their body in fibrous environments. Preprint; the abstract gives few numbers beyond the ten-fold change.
ai_technology: Deep-learning model computing fiber deformation and cell forces from phase microscopy

evidence.tested: Live-cell experiments combined with mathematical modelling.
evidence.unknown: Validation of force accuracy against independent measurements; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning tracked cell movement and fiber deformation to compute forces.
